title: AutoDV: An End-to-End Deep Learning Model for High-Dimensional Data Visualization
claim: Existing visualization methods are highly sensitive to hyperparameter choice, and the best setting varies unpredictably across datasets.
layout: 2 side-by-side heatmaps, shared dataset rows, a colorbar beside each
description: Two side-by-side heatmaps show normalized clustering quality (NMI, scaled per dataset) for nine datasets. The datasets run down the rows: fmnist, mnist, cifar10, Campbell, PBMC68K, Baron Human, Mouse_retina, TUNADROMD and PhiUSIIL. The left panel varies t-SNE perplexity from about 5 to 85. The right panel varies the number of UMAP neighbors from about 3 to 110. A blue-to-red coolwarm scale from 0 to 1 sits to the right of each panel. Smooth, blotchy blobs of red and blue show that the best hyperparameter differs by dataset and changes irregularly. Thin horizontal lines separate the datasets. The eye goes first to the saturated red and blue patches. No method of the authors' own is shown. The figure motivates the need for tuning-free visualization.
caption: NMI Sensitivity under different hyperparameters for t-SNE (perplexity) and UMAP (n neighbor). Note: The datasets are randomly down-sampled to simulate various real-world unseen datasets. Please see details in Appendix I
abstract: High-dimensional data visualization (HDV) plays an important role in data science and engineering applications. Traditional HDV methods, such as Autoencoder and t-SNE, require hyper-parameter tuning and iterative optimization on every dataset and cannot effectively utilize the knowledge from historical low-dimension representation, which lowers the efficiency, convenience, and accuracy in real applications. In this paper, we present AutoDV, an end-to-end deep learning model, for high-dimensional data visualization. AutoDV is built upon a graph transformer network and an invariant loss function and is trained on a number of diverse datasets converted into multi-weight graphs. Given a new dataset, AutoDV outputs the 2D or 3D embeddings of all data points directly. AutoDV has the following merits: 1) There is no hyper-parameter selection during the data visualization stage; 2) The end-to-end model avoids re-training or iterative optimization when visualizing data; 3) The input dataset can have any number of features and can be from any domain. Our experiments show that AutoDV can successfully generalize to unseen datasets without retraining with 89.37\% precision of t-SNE and 91.05\% precision of UMAP on the unseen CIFAR10 datasets. Compared with existing parametric data visualization deep models, our method obtains a significant improvement with 86.65\% precision gain. AutoDV can perform even better than t-SNE and UMAP on gene and UCI tabular datasets. The project is available at https://github.com/DryDew/AutoDV.
